title: Wagner Group forces march on Moscow in a one-day mutiny
body:
On 23 and 24 June 2023, Yevgeny Prigozhin, the leader of the Wagner mercenary group, led an armed rebellion against the Russian military leadership. Prigozhin said he acted after Russia's military attacked his forces and demanded a meeting with the defence minister. He blamed army leaders for failing to supply Wagner fighters in Ukraine with sufficient ammunition.

Wagner fighters took control of military facilities in the southern city of Rostov-on-Don and then advanced north toward Moscow. President Vladimir Putin condemned the revolt as betrayal and treason in a televised address on Saturday, 24 June. Moscow's mayor told residents to avoid travel, and the city cancelled mass outdoor events until 1 July.

Later on 24 June, Wagner halted its advance and fighters left Rostov-on-Don. Negotiations were brokered by Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko. Under the arrangement announced by the Kremlin, the criminal case of armed mutiny against Prigozhin was dropped, Wagner fighters could return to their bases without prosecution, and Prigozhin was to move to Belarus.

The episode was widely described by commentators as a serious challenge to Putin's authority and raised questions about the Russian military's chain of command. Russia had invaded Ukraine in February 2022, and Wagner had taken part in the fighting, including the capture of Bakhmut in May 2023.
